newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Guerrilla war costs Colombia cattlemen $936 mln.
newsitem.headline: Guerrilla war costs Colombia cattlemen $936 mln.

text.p: The fallout from Colombia's simmering internal war and general crime cost cattle-ranchers $936 million in 1996, the head of the National Cattlemen's Federation (Fedegan) said Tuesday.

Jorge Visbal told reporters that 511 cattle-ranchers were among the 1,375 people kidnapped last year, 47 of whom were subsequently murdered. He blamed most of the abductions on the country's Marxist rebels, who fill their war chests with kidnap ransoms.
The cattlemen's leader said the federation's members were also frequent targets of guerrilla extortion demands and sabotage. Cattle rustling added to the losses racked up by ranchers, Visbal said.

"Cattle ranchers lost about $936 million last year. The guerrilla is mostly responsible for these losses. Cattle ranchers are targeted almost exclusively by the guerrillas although often common criminals will carry out the crimes to make it look as if the rebels were not behind them," Visbal told reporters.
Some cattle ranchers themselves admit, however, that they are far from passive bystanders in the conflict.

In the violence-torn northwestern provinces of Antioquia and Cordoba, ranchers recently said they funded right-wing paramilitary groups to lead an unofficial counterinsurgency campaign. Such groups have been blamed for at least 200 murders across Colombia in the last three months.
Carlos Castano, leader of the country's most feared death- squad the so-called Peasant Self Defense Group of Cordoba and Uraba, comes from a cattle-ranching family.
Cattle-ranching is among the sectors that have been hardest hit throughout the three decade long history of Colombia's guerrilla uprising.
